# Complete local transfer at repeated rank-one block zeros

27 October 2026. This is a conditional local theorem for the fixed full
Werner functional. It does not prove its lower-copy premise. No novelty
claim is made.

Write \(H=(\mathbb C^3)^{\otimes m}\), \(L(X)=X-\operatorname{Tr}(X)I_3/2\),
\(q_m(X)=\langle X,L^{\otimes m}X\rangle\), and let \(b_m\) be its
conjugate-linear-first polarization. We use two elementary inherited facts:

\[
 \|L^{\otimes m}\|_{HS\to HS}=1,\qquad
 R_m=\prod_{i=1}^m(I-F_i/2)\succeq\delta I,\quad\delta=2^{-m},
\tag{1}
\]
\[
 b_m(ab^*,cd^*)=\langle a\otimes d,R_m(c\otimes b)\rangle.
\tag{2}
\]

The lower-copy assertion \(W_m\) means \(q_m(Z)\ge0\) for **all complex
rank-at-most-two** \(Z\) on \(H\).

## The local theorem

**Theorem.** Assume \(W_m\). For every nonzero rank-one \(R=uv^*\),
\(C_0=\operatorname{diag}(R,R,0)\) has a neighborhood within the complex
rank-at-most-two variety on which \(q_{m+1}\ge0\). Every zero in a sufficiently
small such neighborhood has a common physical two-plane at the first site:
after one local unitary conjugation its row and column supports at that
site both lie in \(\operatorname{span}(e_0,e_1)\).

Consequently the following are equivalent at each fixed \(m\):

1. \(W_m\).
2. Every nonzero repeated rank-one block zero above is a local minimum of
   \(q_{m+1}\) on rank at most two.
3. The full Hessian at every such zero is positive semidefinite.

The implication 3 to 1 is the already supplied exact lift, and is not a new
induction. The useful addition is 1 to 2, including all degenerate kernel
directions and all orders, with no classification of lower-copy zeros.

Let \(a,b\) range over the six ordered orthogonal pairs consisting of the
two eigenvectors of each Pauli matrix, in both orders. Set \(A=ab^*\).
Direct two-by-two algebra gives

\tag{3}

# Global discriminant and two opposition results

The full all-copy target remains open. This note records what the new
local transfer does not settle. `local_transfer.md` fixes all notation.

## Exact global remaining inequality

For arbitrary first-site factor blocks \(U_0,U_1,X\), \(V_0,V_1,Y\), put
\(U(t)=(U_0,U_1,tX)^T\), \(V(t)=(V_0,V_1,tY)^T\). Every resulting matrix
has rank at most two. The exact splitting is

\[
 q_{m+1}(U(t)V(t)^*)=a+t^2T+\tfrac12t^4d,
\quad a=q_{(2,3,\ldots,3)}(B),\quad d=q_m(XY^*).
\tag{1}
\]

Assuming the complete lower-copy target \(W_m\), both \(a,d\ge0\). Therefore
positivity of (1) for every real \(t\) is equivalent to

\[
 \boxed{\quad T\ge-\sqrt{2ad}.\quad}
\tag{2}
\]

If \(d>0,T<0\), minimize the polynomial in \(z=t^2\) at \(z=-T/d\).
The minimum is \(a-T^2/(2d)\). The cases \(d=0\) or \(T\ge0\) give the
same criterion by inspection. Thus (2), for all the arbitrary complex
two-column blocks, is equivalent to the entire next-copy target under
\(W_m\). It is not proved here. The local theorem proves \(T\ge0\) only in
its specified Gram slice near repeated block zeros.

## Exact failure of global nonnegativity of T, even in a Gram slice

At \(m=1\), use the rational matrices

\[
 U_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\-1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 U_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 V_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&0\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 V_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\-1&0\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
 X=\frac1{41}\begin{pmatrix}41&122\\-35&-246\\-49&-115\end{pmatrix},\quad
 Y=\frac1{41}\begin{pmatrix}83&205\\35&41\\-35&-171\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{3}
\]

They satisfy the two exact Gram slice equations
\(\langle U_i,X\rangle_F+\langle V_i,Y\rangle_F=0\). Direct rational
evaluation using \(q_1(Z)=\|Z\|_F^2-|\operatorname{Tr}Z|^2/2\) gives

\[
 a=67/4,\quad T=-147605/3362<0,\quad d=6714658676/2825761>0.
\tag{4}
\]

Replacing \(X,Y\) by \(X/100,Y/100\) keeps the slice and makes the third
Gram eigenvalue strictly smaller than the two binary eigenvalues. Thus
even the lowest-Gram-line choice does not make \(T\) globally nonnegative.
This is not a negative \(q_2\) witness: (2) is respected. It decisively
blocks extending the local coercivity claim to all gauged factors.

# Warm continuation: a quartic obstruction and a fixed-output global reformulation

27 October 2026. **The all-copy Werner target remains unresolved. No negative witness for a tensor power of the specified Werner state is supplied.** Stage 1 and its frozen copy were preserved. This continuation gives an exact obstruction to extending the block-zero geometry using only generic positivity, then constructs an equivalent full-target reachability formulation. Neither the activation principle nor the general separability reformulation is claimed as new: primary precedents are Vollbrecht--Wolf and Clarisse. The explicit calculations below are reconstructed and checked here; historical priority is unestablished.

Let \(\rho=(2I-F_3)/15\), \(K=I-\Omega_3\Omega_3^*/2\). Thus \(\rho^\Gamma=(2/15)K\). The fixed target is \(q_n(C)\ge0\) for all finite \(n\) and arbitrary complex matrices of rank at most two.

## 1. Strong opposition to the live block-zero route

The stage-1 full Hessian identity extends algebraically to any base Hermitian quadratic form
\[
 q_B(Z)=\langle\operatorname{vec}Z,B\operatorname{vec}Z\rangle,
 \quad R=B^\Gamma,
\]
with the same vectorization and crossed contraction. Define its one-qutrit extension
\[
 Q_B(C)=\langle\operatorname{vec}C,(K\otimes B)\operatorname{vec}C\rangle
       =\sum_{i,j=0}^2q_B(C_{ij})-\tfrac12q_B\Big(\sum_i C_{ii}\Big),
\tag{1}
\]
with physical factors regrouped. We prove a particularly strong local statement when \(B,R\succ0\), then give an exact negative rank-two matrix for that same extended form.

### Local theorem

For every \(N\) and every \(B,B^\Gamma\succ0\) on \(\mathbb C^N\otimes\mathbb C^N\), every point of
\[
 \mathcal M=\{P_E\otimes uv^*: E\in\operatorname{Gr}(2,3),\ u,v\ne0\}
\tag{2}
\]
is a critical zero and a local minimum of \(Q_B\) on the complex rank-two variety. Near this family the zero set is the smooth manifold (2), of real dimension \(4N+2\); the Hessian kernel is exactly its tangent. A single positive neighborhood radius works around the compact family \(\mathcal M_1\) with \(\|uv^*\|_F=1\). This theorem concerns the auxiliary form (1), not the unresolved tensor-power form.
